questions.stem: A technician is accidentally exposed to unshielded germicidal UV-C radiation. Which ocular tissue is expected to absorb most of this short-wavelength exposure before it can reach the retina?
questions.explanation: Short-wavelength UV-C and much UV-B are absorbed predominantly by the cornea and conjunctiva. This is why acute exposure commonly produces photokeratitis and photoconjunctivitis rather than a primary retinal lesion.

questions.explanation: Near-infrared radiation within the retinal hazard region can pass through the ocular media and be concentrated by the eye’s optics onto a small retinal area. A beam can therefore be hazardous even though it is invisible.

questions.stem: A patient views a high-contrast target through progressively smaller pinholes. At the smallest aperture, image quality begins to fall despite reduced aberration. What is the best explanation?
questions.explanation: A small aperture reduces many ocular aberrations, but when it becomes very small diffraction spreads the image and limits resolution.

questions.stem: Why does enlarging the pupil not produce unlimited improvement in spatial resolution?
questions.explanation: A larger aperture reduces diffraction, but rays passing through more peripheral optical zones increase the contribution of ocular aberrations. Image quality reflects a balance between these effects.

questions.stem: A driver reports disabling glare from a wet horizontal road surface. Why can properly oriented polarized sunglasses help?

questions.sampleAnswer: Measure illumination at the inspection plane and determine the critical detail, contrast, belt speed and error consequence. Provide adjustable task lighting or improve contrast so the older worker can see the part without over-brightening the whole room. Shield or relocate the direct luminaire, change the bench finish or lighting geometry to eliminate the reflected image, and replace or repair the flickering source so rotating or moving equipment cannot appear stationary. Add lighting at the point of operation and emergency stop to remove dangerous shadows. Restore tested emergency lighting for the exit route and maintain/clean fixtures. Verify the changes with the worker during the real task. Simply adding more light could intensify glare, reflections and contrast imbalance without correcting flicker or shadows.
